PullRequest.Title: ci: name the Windows Agent Host E2E job after what it runs
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem

Pull request checks can show a skipped `Windows (run)` row with no `/ <job>` suffix and no Linux or macOS counterpart, which looks like a bug.

That row is `windows-agent-host-e2e-tests` (#342735). It skips at the caller when the changes cannot affect the Agent Host E2E tests (`agent-host-e2e` is `false`). GitHub never expands a reusable workflow whose caller is skipped, so the row shows only the caller name, `Windows (run)`, instead of `Windows (run) / Agent-Host-E2E`. For example, #343780 showed `Windows (run) | skipped`.

## Change

- Rename the caller job to `Windows (agent host)`. It now shows as `Windows (agent host) / Agent-Host-E2E` when it runs and as `Windows (agent host)` when it is skipped.
- Update the job name in the `integration-tests` skill and the Agent Host E2E README, and note how the skipped job shows.

Required checks do not change: `required-checks` reports `Windows / Electron` from the job id, not its display name. `job_name` and the 1ES `JobId` do not change either.

## Validation

- From `build/`: `node --test lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts` (10 passed) and `node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts` (7 passed).
- Parsed `pr.yml`: the job name is the static string `Windows (agent host)`, and no other job uses it.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: A pull request whose changes affect Agent Host E2E tests runs the Windows Agent Host CI job.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes must classify the PR, then the windows-agent-host-e2e-tests caller expands pr-win32-test.yml, allocates one Windows runner, restores/builds dependencies, runs the Agent Host E2E suite, uploads logs, and required-checks aggregates the result. The changed `name` is display metadata and is not consumed by this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout the repository, restore dependency caches, and download dependencies/extensions on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequence per affected PR workflow invocation; cache misses can add downloads, but cache keys and invocation count are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reusable workflow, inputs, one runner, checkout, and cache/download steps ran under the caller display name `Windows (run)`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations gate compilation and tests on the Windows Agent Host job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `.\scripts\test-agent-host-e2e.bat`, which starts the selected Agent Host E2E test processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batch command per affected PR job; the existing complete-suite runner executes the selected entrypoints with up to five concurrent processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical command, profile inputs, timeout, and concurrency ran before the display-name change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The test batch is the principal critical-path work before the job can succeed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload logs on every job and crash/node-module artifacts on failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One log upload per job plus up to two failure-only artifact uploads; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same uploads occurred with identical cardinality and payload selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Uploads occur after tests and must finish for job completion, but their conditions and artifact names do not reference the changed caller name.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one Windows Agent Host caller per PR workflow run; selected test entrypoints scale with the existing change-detection profile, not with the renamed display string.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one reusable-workflow invocation is created for this caller and it remains parallel with the separate Windows Electron integration job. The Agent Host suite's existing runner may use up to five test processes; neither caller concurrency nor suite concurrency changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm behavior is unchanged: node_modules uses the existing Windows/architecture key, built-in extensions use the existing hash-derived key, and the static caller display name is absent from cache keys. No new positive, negative, or miss cache state is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff changes only `jobs.windows-agent-host-e2e-tests.name`; the `if`, `uses`, `with` inputs, test command, runner labels, cache keys, and aggregation references remain keyed by the unchanged job id.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub's internal cost of rendering a different short label is not measurable here, but it does not change workflow execution or any realistic scaling input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The same expensive work, cardinality, concurrency, cache behavior, and critical path existed before the PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: A pull request whose changes cannot affect Agent Host E2E tests skips the Windows Agent Host caller.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes completes, the unchanged caller-level `if` evaluates false, and required-checks accepts the skipped result using the unchanged job id and detection output. The renamed caller is only rendered in the checks UI and is off the execution path of the reusable workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout and classify changed files in the Detect Changes job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing detection job per PR workflow run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical detection boundary determined the same unchanged `agent-host-e2e` output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Classification must finish before the caller can be skipped and before required-checks can accept that skip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential reusable Windows workflow dispatch and runner allocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when `agent-host-e2e` is false and detection succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The caller was also skipped before the rename; only its displayed skipped-row label differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No Windows setup, filesystem, network, subprocess, or artifact work occurs for this skipped caller.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One skip decision per PR workflow run, independent of changed-file count after the existing detection job produces its output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The skipped caller expands no reusable workflow and allocates zero Windows runners. The independent required-check matrix behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No Agent Host job cache is read or populated because the caller is skipped. Detection and required-check behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the skip condition and required-check references use the unchanged job id/output, while only the static display name changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; skipped workflow cardinality remains zero.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The rename neither moves work onto the skipped path nor adds a runner, process, I/O call, retained state, or repeated computation.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and the transitive Windows reusable workflow and required-check aggregation. Two files are documentation-only; the sole executable change renames static GitHub Actions display metadata. No performance finding or regression-fix learning signal is warranted.
